# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.

# Figures and the rules behind them (read only; nothing changed)

All the arithmetic is done twice. The Java server works out every figure that is stored or written to the audit file: settled dues, statement totals, closed-period totals, ROLLUP/TOTALS lines and claim-log dues. The TypeScript front end works out every figure the sheet *shows* again from the raw rows. The server never sends a computed due or total to the screen.

## A. Per claim (claim row, `claims.slot.tsx`)

| Shown | Name in code | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| number | `claim_no` / `number` | Set when the claim is opened (`ClaimStatusChange`). By default it's the sheet-wide `sheet.claim_number + 1` (`ClaimRepository.number`). When `numbersPerPeriod` is on (`period_numbering_from` is set and today ≥ it), it's `<period name>-<n>` from a per-period `claim_sequence`, or `X-<n>` when the claim's date is in no period (`numberInPeriod`). A draft has no number. A voided or rejected claim keeps its number, and numbers are never reused. |
| amount, date, note | | `ClaimInput.signedAmount`: two decimals at most, and a negative amount is a correction. A blank date takes the sheet's today. |
| period | `periodOf` | The period whose from–to range (inclusive) contains the claim date. |
| due | `claimDueNow` → `dueNow` (TS), `ClaimRepository.dueNow` (Java) | See the due calculation below. |
| due-by | `due_by` / `ClaimRepository.dueBy` | Set once, at creation: claim date + `terms-<grade>`, using the grade the person has on the claim date and the terms in force on that date, else the sheet's `terms` (14 by default). It is **not recomputed when a draft's date is edited** (`update` doesn't touch it), nor on reassign. |
| overdue | `isOverdue` | OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `dueBy < today`. |
| corrects | `corrects` | Only a negative amount may name a claim, and a negative amount must name one: a SETTLED claim of the same person, by number (`checkCorrection`). |
| stated | `stated` | Set when the last statement bound the claim. `isBound`/`bound()` = stated **and not PENDING**. |
| status | DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED, VOID | See the status rules below. |
| opened-by | `opened_by` | Set when the claim is opened. |
| deferred / deferred-until | `isDeferred`, SQL `deferred` column | Status OPEN and `deferredUntil > today`. Deferred-until is only shown while the claim is deferred. |
| log lines | `claim_log` / `ClaimRepository.log` | `<STATUS> by <user> on <today> due=<dueNow or n/a>`, written when the claim is added and on each status change or re-settle. |

### How a claim's due is worked out (`figure` → `due` → `dueNow`)
1. **Fixed figure** (`figure` / `fixedDue`), checked in this order:
   - the settled due (`settled_due`);
   - else, if bound, n/a when `stated_na`;
   - else, if bound, `stated_due`;
   - else the live due.
2. **Live due** (`due`): amount × rate% / 100.
   - The rate is `RATE_ON` / `rateFor`: the rate for the grade the person had **on the claim date** (`GRADE_ON` / `gradeOn`) with the latest from-date on or before the claim date. An undated rate applies from the beginning of time.
   - If that rate's to-date is before the claim date, the result is **n/a**. It does not fall back to an earlier rate.
   - It is rounded to 2 decimals by the claim's rounding mode (step 3).
   - It is then raised to at least the `floor` in force on the claim date (1.00 by default). A correction gets no floor.
3. **Rounding** (`rounding` / `roundsHalfUp`): half up when the claim date is before `policy_date` (a blank policy date means the sheet's today), otherwise half-even. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects.
4. **Late charge** (`dueNow` / `withCharge`):
   - It applies only while the claim is OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and not a correction.
   - Charge = figure × `late-pct` (in force on the **claim date**, 0.00 by default) × ⌊(today − dueBy) / 30⌋. It is rounded by the same rounding mode.
   - A statement never binds the charge. Settling freezes it in.

## B. Per person (person row)

| Shown (testid) | Where it's computed | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `person-grade` | `PersonRepository.GRADE_TODAY` | The grade in force on the sheet's today. Grades are dated (`person_grade`). The first grade has no from-date. |
| `person-claimed` | `claimed()` (TS), `Rollup.take` (Java) | Sum of the amounts of the claims that **count**. Corrections are included, so they subtract. (The TS version uses float→cent rounding; everything else uses exact cents.) |
| `person-due-total` | `useDueFigures` (TS), `Rollup.take` / `TakeStatement` (Java) | Sum of `dueNow` over the counting claims, skipping n/a, then `capped` at the `cap` in force on **today**. It shows **n/a** unless one of these is true: a rate for today's grade is in force today (`rated`), or some counting claim has a fixed figure, or some counting claim has a due. |
| `person-excess` | `useExcess` (TS only) | Uncapped sum − cap when that is positive, else 0.00. |
| `person-period-<name>-due-total` | `usePersonPeriodDueTotals` | Sum of `dueNow` over the counting claims dated in the period. It is **not capped**. Once the period is closed it shows the frozen `period_person_total` (0.00 for a person added since). |
| `person-overdue-count` / `-total` | `useOverdue` | Counting claims that are overdue, and the sum of their `dueNow`. |
| statement count, stated total, statement date | `TakeStatement` → `person.statement_count`, `stated_total`, `statement_date` | Stored when a statement is taken. |
| `person-hold`, hold lines | `Person.held` | "yes" if the person has **any** hold row, including holds that have already ended. |
| `person-retired`, retired-from | `retired_from` | Any date set counts as retired straight away, even a future date. |
| `person-patrons`, `person-backing` | `patrons.slot.tsx` (TS only) | Backing = the patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a. |

### Which claims count (`Claim.counts(holds)` / `counts()`)
A claim counts if it is SETTLED, **or** it is OPEN/PENDING, not deferred, and either bound by a statement or not dated inside one of the person's holds (`Hold.covers`: both ends inclusive, with null meaning open-ended). DRAFT and VOID claims never count.

## C. Sheet-wide figures

- **Claimed total, due total, overdue total and overdue count**: the person figures added up, skipping n/a. These show in the rollup lines and again in the header.
- **`summary-grade-X-count` / `-due-total`**: people whose grade today is X, **leaving out retired people**.
- **`header-people-count`**: everyone, including retired people.
- **Status counts** (`countWithStatus`): a straight count of claims by status. The comment "no claim is PENDING today" is stale.
- **Period due-total**: the sum of the per-person period totals, or the stored `closed_total` once the period is closed.
- **`rate-current-X`**: `rateFor(grade, today)`, or n/a.
- **Current settings**: `settingOn(key, today)`. The policy date and period-numbering date are not dated settings.

## D. What is frozen, and when

- **Settle / approve** stores `dueNow` (late charge included) in `settled_due`. If the claim had no rate, nothing is stored and its due **stays live**.
- **Re-settle** (stewards only) recomputes the claim as an unbound OPEN claim using today's rates, grades, floor and late charge.
- **Statement** (`TakeStatement`):
  - Each counting claim is bound to its `figure`. If the claim has no figure because its rate has ended (`rateEnded`), it is bound to n/a for good (`stated_na`).
  - Claims that don't count are unbound.
  - PENDING claims are stored as stated but are not treated as bound.
  - The person's capped due-total and the date are stored.
- **Close period** (`ClosePeriod`) stores the uncapped period total and each person's period total. **Reopen** (stewards only) deletes them.
- **Reassign** clears the claim's statement binding.

## E. Status rules and who may do what (`ClaimStatusChange`, `SettingsRepository.role`)

- Allowed transitions:
  - open: DRAFT → OPEN
  - settle: OPEN → SETTLED
  - approve: PENDING → SETTLED
  - reject: PENDING → OPEN, and a reason is required
  - void: DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING → VOID
  - defer: OPEN only, and only to a date after today
- **Four eyes**: the user who opened a claim cannot settle or approve it.
- **Clerk limit**: a clerk's settle goes to **PENDING** when `dueNow > clerkLimit` (the limit in force today; n/a is within any limit). Stewards settle outright.
- **Steward only**: approve, reject, re-settle, reassign and reopen a period. A user not listed in `sheet_role` is a clerk.
- **No role check on saving roles or settings.** A clerk can make themselves a steward. Adding, closing, retiring, holding, statements and rates are also open to anyone.
- **Bulk open / bulk settle** run the single-claim rules for each claim, count refusals, and sort the claims by person id and then claim id descending. That doesn't quite match the displayed `listed` order once a claim has been reassigned.
- **Only DRAFT claims can be edited.** The client also refuses an edit without asking the server.

## F. What dates decide

- **Sheet `today`** stands in for the real date everywhere: default dates, overdue, deferral, the grade/rate check that decides n/a, cap, clerk limit, the policy date when blank, and when period numbering starts.
- **The claim date** chooses the grade, rate, floor, late %, terms and rounding for that claim.
- **`PeriodGuard.open`** refuses any change to a claim dated inside a closed period: add, edit (both old and new date), every status action, defer, reassign and re-settle. Statements, rates, holds and today changes are **not** guarded; they can change live figures, but closed totals are already frozen.
- **`claimAllowed`**: no claim may be dated *after* the person's retired-from date. Claims on that date are allowed.

## G. Imports and shortcuts

- **Paste** (`PasteClaims`): one `name,amount,date,note` per line, the name matched ignoring case.
  - All lines are checked before any is written, and a refusal reports the line number.
  - Each line becomes a DRAFT claim and gets its own CLAIM_ADDED and rollup lines.
  - `corrects` is always null, so **any negative pasted amount is refused**.
- **Quick-add**: the amount must not be negative. The claim is dated today. The person is created with grade A if the name is new. The closed-period and retired checks run first.

## H. Audit side effects

- Every change writes its event line.
- `Rollup.record` then writes a ROLLUP line for each person whose claimed, due-total or overdue-total moved, plus a TOTALS line when the sheet totals moved.
- Changing today writes only rollup lines.

---

# 2. How hard was it to follow?

Hard. The rules are scattered and duplicated. The due, rounding, floor, late-charge, "counts" and n/a logic is written once in Java (`ClaimRepository`, `Claim`, `Rollup`, `TakeStatement`, `ClosePeriod`) and again in TypeScript (`useRates`, `useOverdue`, `useClaims`, `useDueTotals`, `usePeriodDueTotals`). Status, role and period checks are spread across about 15 pipeline step classes, so the long doc comments are the only spec. Some of those comments are already wrong:
- The V7 migration and the TS `Claim` type say voiding clears the number; the code keeps it.
- `statusCounts` says no claim is PENDING.

A new developer would have to read both stacks side by side to be sure what a figure on screen means.

   - A statement never binds the charge. Settling freezes it in.

## B. Per person (person row)

| Shown (testid) | Where it's computed | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `person-grade` | `PersonRepository.GRADE_TODAY` | The grade in force on the sheet's today. Grades are dated (`person_grade`). The first grade has no from-date. |
| `person-claimed` | `claimed()` (TS), `Rollup.take` (Java) | Sum of the amounts of the claims that **count**. Corrections are included, so they subtract. (The TS version uses float→cent rounding; everything else uses exact cents.) |
| `person-due-total` | `useDueFigures` (TS), `Rollup.take` / `TakeStatement` (Java) | Sum of `dueNow` over the counting claims, skipping n/a, then `capped` at the `cap` in force on **today**. It shows **n/a** unless one of these is true: a rate for today's grade is in force today (`rated`), or some counting claim has a fixed figure, or some counting claim has a due. |
| `person-excess` | `useExcess` (TS only) | Uncapped sum − cap when that is positive, else 0.00. |
| `person-period-<name>-due-total` | `usePersonPeriodDueTotals` | Sum of `dueNow` over the counting claims dated in the period. It is **not capped**. Once the period is closed it shows the frozen `period_person_total` (0.00 for a person added since). |
| `person-overdue-count` / `-total` | `useOverdue` | Counting claims that are overdue, and the sum of their `dueNow`. |
| statement count, stated total, statement date | `TakeStatement` → `person.statement_count`, `stated_total`, `statement_date` | Stored when a statement is taken. |
| `person-hold`, hold lines | `Person.held` | "yes" if the person has **any** hold row, including holds that have already ended. |
| `person-retired`, retired-from | `retired_from` | Any date set counts as retired straight away, even a future date. |
| `person-patrons`, `person-backing` | `patrons.slot.tsx` (TS only) | Backing = the patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a. |

### Which claims count (`Claim.counts(holds)` / `counts()`)
A claim counts if it is SETTLED, **or** it is OPEN/PENDING, not deferred, and either bound by a statement or not dated inside one of the person's holds (`Hold.covers`: both ends inclusive, with null meaning open-ended). DRAFT and VOID claims never count.

## C. Sheet-wide figures

- **Claimed total, due total, overdue total and overdue count**: the person figures added up, skipping n/a. These show in the rollup lines and again in the header.
- **`summary-grade-X-count` / `-due-total`**: people whose grade today is X, **leaving out retired people**.
- **`header-people-count`**: everyone, including retired people.
- **Status counts** (`countWithStatus`): a straight count of claims by status. The comment "no claim is PENDING today" is stale.
- **Period due-total**: the sum of the per-person period totals, or the stored `closed_total` once the period is closed.
- **`rate-current-X`**: `rateFor(grade, today)`, or n/a.
- **Current settings**: `settingOn(key, today)`. The policy date and period-numbering date are not dated settings.

## D. What is frozen, and when

- **Settle / approve** stores `dueNow` (late charge included) in `settled_due`. If the claim had no rate, nothing is stored and its due **stays live**.
- **Re-settle** (stewards only) recomputes the claim as an unbound OPEN claim using today's rates, grades, floor and late charge.
- **Statement** (`TakeStatement`):
  - Each counting claim is bound to its `figure`. If the claim has no figure because its rate has ended (`rateEnded`), it is bound to n/a for good (`stated_na`).
  - Claims that don't count are unbound.
  - PENDING claims are stored as stated but are not treated as bound.
  - The person's capped due-total and the date are stored.
- **Close period** (`ClosePeriod`) stores the uncapped period total and each person's period total. **Reopen** (stewards only) deletes them.
- **Reassign** clears the claim's statement binding.

## E. Status rules and who may do what (`ClaimStatusChange`, `SettingsRepository.role`)

- Allowed transitions:
  - open: DRAFT → OPEN
  - settle: OPEN → SETTLED
  - approve: PENDING → SETTLED
  - reject: PENDING → OPEN, and a reason is required
  - void: DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING → VOID
  - defer: OPEN only, and only to a date after today
- **Four eyes**: the user who opened a claim cannot settle or approve it.
- **Clerk limit**: a clerk's settle goes to **PENDING** when `dueNow > clerkLimit` (the limit in force today; n/a is within any limit). Stewards settle outright.
- **Steward only**: approve, reject, re-settle, reassign and reopen a period. A user not listed in `sheet_role` is a clerk.
- **No role check on saving roles or settings.** A clerk can make themselves a steward. Adding, closing, retiring, holding, statements and rates are also open to anyone.
- **Bulk open / bulk settle** run the single-claim rules for each claim, count refusals, and sort the claims by person id and then claim id descending. That doesn't quite match the displayed `listed` order once a claim has been reassigned.
- **Only DRAFT claims can be edited.** The client also refuses an edit without asking the server.

## F. What dates decide

- **Sheet `today`** stands in for the real date everywhere: default dates, overdue, deferral, the grade/rate check that decides n/a, cap, clerk limit, the policy date when blank, and when period numbering starts.
- **The claim date** chooses the grade, rate, floor, late %, terms and rounding for that claim.
- **`PeriodGuard.open`** refuses any change to a claim dated inside a closed period: add, edit (both old and new date), every status action, defer, reassign and re-settle. Statements, rates, holds and today changes are **not** guarded; they can change live figures, but closed totals are already frozen.
- **`claimAllowed`**: no claim may be dated *after* the person's retired-from date. Claims on that date are allowed.

## G. Imports and shortcuts

- **Paste** (`PasteClaims`): one `name,amount,date,note` per line, the name matched ignoring case.
  - All lines are checked before any is written, and a refusal reports the line number.
  - Each line becomes a DRAFT claim and gets its own CLAIM_ADDED and rollup lines.
  - `corrects` is always null, so **any negative pasted amount is refused**.
- **Quick-add**: the amount must not be negative. The claim is dated today. The person is created with grade A if the name is new. The closed-period and retired checks run first.

## H. Audit side effects

- Every change writes its event line.
- `Rollup.record` then writes a ROLLUP line for each person whose claimed, due-total or overdue-total moved, plus a TOTALS line when the sheet totals moved.
- Changing today writes only rollup lines.

# 2. How hard was it to follow?

Hard. The rules are scattered and duplicated. The due, rounding, floor, late-charge, "counts" and n/a logic is written once in Java (`ClaimRepository`, `Claim`, `Rollup`, `TakeStatement`, `ClosePeriod`) and again in TypeScript (`useRates`, `useOverdue`, `useClaims`, `useDueTotals`, `usePeriodDueTotals`). Status, role and period checks are spread across about 15 pipeline step classes, so the long doc comments are the only spec. Some of those comments are already wrong:
- The V7 migration and the TS `Claim` type say voiding clears the number; the code keeps it.
- `statusCounts` says no claim is PENDING.

A new developer would have to read both stacks side by side to be sure what a figure on screen means.
